expectations.text: Uses cdkTrapFocus or CdkTrapFocus directive from @angular/cdk/a11y for focus trapping
expectations.evidence: The dialog template uses `cdkTrapFocus` and `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture` directives on the inner dialog div. `A11yModule` is imported from `@angular/cdk/a11y` in the component's `imports` array.

expectations.text: Dialog has role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' or uses the native <dialog> element
expectations.evidence: The dialog div has `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` as static attributes in the template.

expectations.text: Focus moves to the dialog on open (autoFocus or programmatic focus)
expectations.evidence: `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture` is set on the dialog container. The explanation section confirms: 'Combined with `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"`, the CDK `FocusTrap` calls `focusInitialElementWhenReady()` immediately after the component is attached to the DOM.'

expectations.text: Escape key closes the dialog via keyboard event handler
expectations.evidence: `@HostListener('document:keydown.escape') onEscape(): void { this.cancel(); }` is present in `ConfirmationDialogComponent`.

expectations.text: Focus returns to the trigger element after dialog closes
expectations.evidence: In `confirmation-dialog.service.ts`, the `open()` method accepts `trigger: HTMLElement` and calls `trigger.focus()` inside a `finalize` operator that runs on both confirm and cancel paths. `ConfirmButtonDirective` passes `inject(ElementRef).nativeElement` as the trigger automatically.

expectations.text: Background content uses the inert attribute or aria-hidden='true'
expectations.evidence: `setInertOnBackgroundContent(true)` is called in `ngOnInit`, which sets the HTML `inert` attribute on every direct child of `<body>` except the CDK overlay container. It is removed in `ngOnDestroy`.
`changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` is present in the `@Component` decorator of `ConfirmationDialogComponent`.

expectations.text: Has aria-labelledby or aria-label for the dialog title
expectations.evidence: The dialog div has `[attr.aria-labelledby]="titleId"` binding, which points to the `<h2>` element rendered with `[id]="titleId"`. The `titleId` is a stable unique string generated at construction time.

claims.claim: Focus moves to the Cancel button first because it is first in DOM order and CDK focuses the first focusable element
claims.evidence: Cancel button appears before the Confirm button in the template, and `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture` focuses the first focusable element. The explanation notes this is intentional to protect against reflexive Enter presses on destructive actions.

claims.claim: Background content is made inert via `setInertOnBackgroundContent` targeting direct children of `<body>`
claims.evidence: The helper function is implemented and called in `ngOnInit`/`ngOnDestroy`. It queries `.cdk-overlay-container` and sets/removes `inert` on all other body children.

claims.claim: The CDK overlay host is automatically added to the DOM by `OverlayContainer`
claims.evidence: This is standard CDK behavior and consistent with the implementation shown.

claims.claim: The `@Input`/`@Output` decorators are used in `ConfirmButtonDirective` rather than the `input()`/`output()` signal functions
claims.evidence: The directive uses `@Input('appConfirmButton')` and `@Output() confirmed = new EventEmitter<boolean>()`. The project's code style mandates `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators per AGENTS.md. This is a style violation in the generated code, though it does not affect the accessibility expectations being graded.

claims.claim: HostListener is used in `ConfirmButtonDirective` rather than the `host` object
claims.evidence: `@HostListener('click')` is used in `ConfirmButtonDirective`. Project style mandates using the `host` object in `@Component`/`@Directive` decorators instead. Minor style violation, not covered by the graded expectations.

suggestions.assertion: Focus moves to the dialog on open (autoFocus or programmatic focus)
suggestions.reason: Using `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture` satisfies this assertion, but it is CDK doing the work via attribute binding — not a custom `autoFocus` input or explicit `ElementRef.nativeElement.focus()` call. A tighter assertion might require verifying that focus actually lands inside the dialog element (e.g., by checking for an explicit `focusTrap.focusInitialElement()` call or a unit test assertion), since the attribute alone does not prove the browser actually moves focus.

No assertion checks that the implementation does not use the deprecated `@Input`/`@Output` decorators or `@HostListener` in directives. The `ConfirmButtonDirective` violates the project's mandated code style (`input()`/`output()` signal functions, `host` object instead of `@HostListener`). These are observable in the output but not caught by any expectation.

No assertion verifies that `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` is also set on the `AppComponent` usage example. The component file sets it, but the example `AppComponent` also sets it — worth noting the eval only checks the dialog component, which is the relevant target.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 expectations are well-targeted and correctly pass. The strongest gap is the absence of a style-compliance assertion: the generated directive code uses deprecated `@Input`/`@Output` decorators and `@HostListener` instead of the project-mandated signal-based `input()`/`output()` and `host` object. This is visible in the output but unchecked by any eval.
